text:
emma: FYI — we just got a legal ping asking how fast we can honor a customer data deletion for telemetry. current exporter topology makes this non-trivial.

raj: ugh. which exporter path? hosted, dedicated, or private?

emma: hosted for now, but we should design the API & routing so Dedicated/Private can opt-in. main pain is that spans get fanout to multiple downstreams (s3, bigquery, long-term cold store).

sasha: can we namespace by customer id at ingest and keep that as first-class routing key? that would let us drop/retention per-namespace.

aleks: agreed. proposal: enforce a single immutable namespace tag on all spans: customer.namespace = cust_<id>. route/exporter would be keyed by that value.

priya: that helps for routing. question: what about pre-aggregated traces and derived metrics? deletion needs to sweep those too.

emma: yep. we sketched a lifecycle: 1) mark dataset deleted 2) block new writes to namespace 3) trigger delete job for hot/nearline stores 4) schedule cold-store tombstone + audit log.

raj: timeline wise — legal wants 7 days. we probably can do hot-store purge in hours, but cold-store may be weeks unless we change retention policy. do we have SLA/contract implications?

sasha: we could offer "accelerated deletion" as an enterprise option: on-demand cold-store sweep for a fee, otherwise default retention applies. but need RBAC and an API.

emma: proposed internal API (example):
```
POST /internal/telemetry/v1/purge
Body: {"customer_id":"cust_123","before":"2024-01-01T00:00:00Z","scope":["hot","nearline","cold"]}
```
Response: job id.

aleks: add safety: require org-admin token + signed delete request + audit-entry. also propagate deletion to exporters: we need exporter contracts to accept a purge op.

priya: exporters will need a small control channel. sample config mapping: 
```
routes:
  - namespace: "cust_<id>"
    exporters:
      - s3://redwood-telemetry/customers/cust_<id>/
    retention_days: 90
    rbac_principals: ["org-admins:cust_<id>"]
```

raj: how do we avoid tons of tiny S3 prefixes? cost/manifest explosion. maybe bundle small customers into shard buckets but keep an index mapping for deletion.

sasha: index mapping is fine: keep control-plane manifest SLOW_PATH that maps namespace->(bucket,object_prefix,shard_key). when purge happens we consult mapping and delete matching objects. this avoids creating thousands of buckets.

policy-bot: scheduled retention sweep completed for namespace cust_987 — removed 12M objects, 7.4GB freed :white_check_mark:

emma: UX questions for console: we should show deletion job status, estimated time, scope selection (hot/nearline/cold), and show what will remain if any. also a dry-run mode.

priya: UX note — make the default deletion permission only for "org-admins" and surface consequences (billing, analytics gaps). include an audit trail link in the job details.

aleks: ops: we need to define backpressure and rate limits for purge jobs — otherwise huge deletes will hammer exporters and storage APIs. maybe token-bucket with configurable throughput per customer.

raj: rollout plan: start with read-only namespace tagging + retention metadata for 2 weeks, then add purge API in beta for enterprise accounts, then export control channel and per-exporter purge handlers.

emma: agree. I'll write a short RFC with these pieces (ingest namespace, control API, exporter contract, console UX, rate limiting). want volunteers for reviewer loop?

sasha: I can review exporter contract and index mapping.

aleks: I'll take the control API and RBAC bits.

priya: happy to do Console job UX and audit trail design.

raj: I'll coordinate with infra and billing on shard strategy and cost implications.

emma: great. I'll drop the RFC link here when ready. thanks all. :raised_hands:
